response.message:
═══════════════════════════════════════
           COMMAND REFERENCE
═══════════════════════════════════════

MILITARY COMMANDS:
  attack     - Engage enemy forces or capture region
               "Ney, attack Mack" / "attack" (nearest)

  defend     - Take defensive position (+30% bonus)
               "Davout, defend" / "hold" (alias)

  move       - Move to adjacent region
               "Lannes, move to Munich"

  retreat    - Fall back toward friendly territory (FREE)
               "Ney, retreat" - Aggressive marshals may object!

  recruit    - Raise troops (1 Admin AP + gold)
               "recruit" / "recruit for Davout" / "recruit at Paris"
               Infantry 10k / Cavalry 5k / Artillery 3k, from the
               manpower pools. PRICING: base 200-400g, capital -25%,
               x3 AT WAR, dearer above the FORCE LIMIT, and the
               marshal's administration prices the levy (Davout -15%,
               Murat +15% - his card explains, press G).
  substitutes - "buy substitutes for Ney" (1 Admin AP + gold)
               "purchase a levy for Ney" / "hire replacements for Ney"
               The remplacant: under the
               conscription law a called-up man could pay another
               to serve in his place. Draws NO men from the pools -
               gold alone - so it is the one purchase your TREASURY
               limits rather than your class. It is dear, and it
               grows dearer as the class empties. Two limits Berthier
               will name for you: substitutes are received only on
               ground WE hold, and a marshal in the field takes them
               in a smaller draft than one at a depot. You may buy up
               to the point where keeping the men turns punitive, and
               not a man past it. Replacements, never expansion -
               and green men dilute a veteran corps' morale.

  bombardment - Artillery fires on adjacent region (max 2/turn)
               "bombard Swabia" - Cannot fire after moving.

  garrison   - Leave detachment to defend a region (2 AP)
               Max 3 garrisons per nation. Fights to destruction.

TACTICAL COMMANDS:
  fortify    - Dig in for growing defense; cannot move/attack
               "Davout, fortify" (his Iron Resolve coils +8%/turn here)
  unfortify  - Abandon fortifications (immediate)
  drill      - Train for +20% attack, one charge (2 turns; Soult's
               Drillmaster finishes in 1) - "Soult, drill"
  scout      - Reconnaissance: "scout Tyrol" / "Davout, scout"
  form square - Anti-cavalry square: cavalry -40% damage, but
               artillery +50%. Breaks on any other order.
  break square - Return to line (FREE)

STANCE COMMANDS:
  aggressive - +15% attack, -10% defense ("Ney, go aggressive")
  defensive  - -10% attack, +15% defense
  neutral    - Balanced (default, FREE to return)

STRATEGIC COMMANDS (2 AP, multi-turn):
  march      - "Ney, march to Vienna" - travels over several turns
  pursue     - "Murat, pursue Kutuzov" - chase across the map
  support    - "Lannes, support Ney" - march to an ally's battles
  hold       - "Davout, hold Swabia" - hold ground (artillery auto-fires)
  cancel     - "cancel Ney" / "halt Ney" (1 AP)

TWO ORDERS IN ONE LINE:
  then attack - "Ney, march to Swabia then attack Mack" - the ONE
               two-step order the engine holds: he marches, and
               engages the named man (or whoever holds the ground)
               on arrival. Paid once, at 2 AP.
  , then ...  - "Ney, scout Swabia, then fortify" - any other pair
               is TWO orders: the first goes out, the second is
               handed back to your command line for your seal (it
               pays its own AP when you send it). A second order
               that would UNDO the first - attack after fortify,
               march before his march is done - is named, not
               filled: give it when you mean it.
  until ...   - "Davout, hold Lorraine until Ney arrives" - a hold
               that ends when a named marshal of ours reaches him;
               also 'until relieved', 'until the battle is won',
               'for 3 turns'. 'when / once / as soon as Ney
               arrives, hold Lorraine' is read the same way and
               says so. A hold that waits for a man not on the
               board, for no turns, or for a turn behind us is
               refused, free.
  or / and    - "Davout, hold Lorraine until Ney arrives or the battle
               is won" ends on whichever comes first; 'and' means
               BOTH must land, and the Ledger ticks each off as it
               does. 'for 2 turns' counts the turn you give it.
  NOTE: orders are never held for a later turn - there is no queue.
        'hold until ...' is the standing order; everything else you
        give on the morning you want it carried.

ECONOMY (Admin AP - the new imperial economy):
  economy    - Treasury report: income, upkeep, occupation costs,
               dotations, manpower pools ("economy" / "treasury")
  build      - "build market at Paris" (1 AP) - also fortification,
               stables, training ground, supply depot, watchtower
  repair     - "repair Lorraine" (1 AP, 150g)
  endow      - "Endow Ney with the Duchy of Swabia" (1 AP)
               Grants a CONQUERED province to a marshal as his
               ESTATE: its full income becomes his, permanently.
               First estate = 200g investiture; more are fee-free.
               Victories raise a marshal's EXPECTATION of reward -
               leave it unmet and his loyalty erodes each turn.
               Estates never pay occupation costs, and they GROW:
               an able administrator's estates (admin 8+) stabilize
               faster; a wasteful lord's (3-) decay.
  rente      - "Grant Ney a rente" (1 AP) / "Revoke Ney's rente"
               The treasury alternative to land: a pension sized to
               his current shortfall. Safe from war and instantly
               available anywhere - but it costs the crown HALF
               AGAIN its face each turn, never grows, and buys no
               title. Re-grant after new victories to top it up.
               (On the Generals screen - press G - each marshal's
               card shows his reward state; the [ Reward... ] button
               appears there once he has EARNED an unmet expectation.)

  THE IMPERIAL BOOKS (press T for the full ledger):
  - Upkeep: 8g per 1,000 troops. Armies over your FORCE LIMIT pay
    up to double on the excess; the limit grows with territory.
  - Occupation: conquered provinces bleed gold by stability tier -
    secure and stabilize them to cut the bill. Homeland is free.
  - Capturing a province holding an enemy marshal's estate offers
    CONFISCATE (gold windfall + his lasting grudge) or RESPECT.

THE ADMIRALTY (the wooden wall - press T, then 7; every order below
is a button there, with its terms, so none of it need be typed):
  build ships - "build ships" / "lay down a ship" (1 Admin AP +
               400g). 2 keels/turn at most - 1 under blockade.
               New crews come aboard GREEN; only sea-time drills
               a navy. Ships are laid down in a yard we control.
  blockade   - "blockade the enemy" (1 AP) - the fleet closes an
               at-war enemy's ports where our sail outmatches
               hers (1.25x her effective strength): her trade
               halves and her crews rot at anchor. A court we
               cannot outmatch is not closed, and a fleet that is
               itself blockaded does not drill. The Admiralty
               board names both, court by court.
  guard      - "guard home waters" (1 AP) - cover every crossing
               that touches our own coast.
  land       - land <marshal> in <province> (2 AP) - a small
               expedition (15,000 men or fewer, embarking at one of
               our yards or from a foreign shore) slips past the
               patrols at QUOTED odds; Ireland is reachable, an
               army is not. At the 1805 opening only the Guard is
               under the lift, and the Emperor does not sail - a
               newly commissioned marshal's 5,000 is the road;
               THE ADMIRALTY names him and his price.
               A neutral shore must RECEIVE us (a friend, ally or
               vassal); an enemy's needs no leave. Click a coastal
               province on the map for the landing chip.
  NOTE: an army never MARCHES onto a defended enemy coast - while
        any hostile fleet watches the water, a hostile shore is
        taken by expedition or not at all. Sink the covering fleet
        and the crossing becomes an open ferry.
  diversion  - "order the diversion" (1 AP, once per war) - the
               fleet draws the enemy off station: succeed and the
               Strait lies open two turns; fail and be brought to
               battle coming home.
  - An army cannot walk a sea crossing a hostile fleet commands -
    the map draws a shut strait CRIMSON, an open window GOLD, and
    a DEFENDED SHORE (the water is ours, the far coast is not)
    AMBER: that shore is taken by expedition, never by marching.

DIPLOMACY - THE CABINET IS THE DOOR (press F1):
  Matters of state are conducted at the table, not by dispatch.
  Press F1 (or click [Diplomacy]) for the Cabinet: pick a court,
  and every treaty, war, mission, vassal matter and design lies
  there with its price and its odds stated.
  assess     - "Talleyrand, assess our situation" stays spoken
               (the war room - fronts, threats, counsel; free);
               "Talleyrand, assess Austria" for one nation.
  vassals    - the VASSALS tab of the Strategic Ledger (T) carries
               invest / autonomy / release chips per satellite;
               ceding conquered land is in the Cabinet's court page.
  war terms  - open the war banner on the left and press
               [Request Terms] to make the enemy name a price.
  missions   - F1, a court, then its mission row. Talleyrand goes in
               person and works every turn you can pay him; one
               mission at a time.
                 Improve Relations - 1 DP a turn
                   +8 relation/turn
                 Court - 2 DP a turn
                   +8 relation/turn, proposals +2/turn courted (max +10), 20% blowback
                 Reassure Ally - 1 DP a turn (a full alliance only)
                   +4 relation/turn
                 Undermine Alliance - 2 DP a turn
                   -4 relation between targets/turn
                 Gather Intel - 1 DP a turn
                   3 turns, then full intel for 5
               Relations drift 1 a turn toward the calm band (a truce
               thaws faster); the court he courts does not cool while
               he is there. Sending a proposal takes him away: the
               mission costs nothing and earns nothing until he
               returns. Watch it in the Strategic Ledger's Orders tab
               (T) or on its notice; recall him from either, free.
  THE COMPACTS - three instruments that shipped and were never
               named here, so no player could learn they exist:
  buy off    - "buy off Prussia" - a court aims a grievance at us;
               gold buys its SLEEP for a term. The price is stated
               before you offer (D4 - diplomacy has no fog), and it
               is read off how badly they want the thing.
  sponsor    - "sponsor Prussia against Austria, 200 gold" - arm
               somebody else's grievance, per turn, for a term.
               "license Prussia against Austria" at no gold sells
               permission instead: the same bond, a cheaper coin.
               Talleyrand refuses to aim a design at ourselves.
  guarantee  - "guarantee Saxony" - pledge to defend a border.
               Coveters read the pledge and want it less; abandon
               it and the grievance is ours to answer for.
  NOTE: a standing compact runs its TERM. There is no cancelling
        it - war on the court, or a pledge that contradicts it,
        is a RENEGE, and Europe remembers who broke a word.

  Press D for the Diplomatic Ledger - all twenty nations of Europe,
  treaties, wars, and the Balance of Europe.

THE CONGRESS OF PARIS (how the reign is WON - the table of the
great powers is the Diplomatic Ledger's Congress tab, press D then 7):
  summon     - "summon the congress" (1 Admin AP + 2 DP), or the
               Congress of Paris row atop the Cabinet (F1). It needs
               50 TITLED provinces - homeland, ceded by treaty, a
               client's soil, or held 12 quiet turns - with Paris
               held, the Emperor free and no satellite on the brink.
               It cannot be undone. For 8 turns every great power
               answers - RECOGNIZES, REFUSES, SUES, SHUT OUT or GONE -
               with its reason and its PRICE. Keep the 50, Paris and
               the Emperor's freedom, and declare no war: on the
               eighth turn, with every great power won over, shut out
               or gone, the Imperial Peace is signed. Otherwise the
               Congress dissolves, and may be summoned again after
               10 turns.
  sweetener  - "offer Prussia 1000 gold for recognition" - offer
               <court> <gold> gold for recognition, at the table
               while the Congress sits (1 DP): +10 for every 1,000
               gold, at most +20 a court. Gold past that is not taken.
  Ask before you act - "can we summon the congress?" names every
  term still unmet, and nothing is spent.

SCREENS & HOTKEYS:
  F1 diplomacy wizard | T strategic ledger | G marshals
  D diplomatic ledger | L campaign log | R morning dispatch
  E end turn | Tab terminal

YOUR MARSHALS (press G - each card shows skills, trust, ability):
  Ney "Bravest of the Brave" - devastating assaults
  Davout "Iron Resolve" - fortified patience becomes a hammer-blow
  Soult "Drillmaster of Boulogne" - sharpens his corps in a day
  Lannes "Roland of the Army" - marches to the sound of the guns
  Murat "First Horseman of Europe" - turns routs into annihilation
  Bernadotte "Eyes on a Crown" - may not march for you at all
  Massena "Child of Victory" - hardest to kill when outnumbered
  Enemy generals carry famed abilities too - intel will name them.

GLORY AND GRIEVANCE (the ladder on the Generals screen):
  Victories earn GLORY, counted over the last 8 turns. A marshal who
  falls behind a peer starts to ENVY him - and once he does, that man
  stays his rival for as long as he is above.
  ESTATES AND RENTES CANNOT TOUCH THIS. Gold answers a marshal's
  LOYALTY; only glory answers his envy. Rewarding a jealous marshal
  is not wrong - it is simply a different quarrel.
  A grievance costs you a corps: he will not coordinate with the man
  he resents, and at the worst he will not march beside him at all.
  Watch the muster preview - it names the quarrel when it bites.
  What ENDS it is the field. An aggressive marshal needs a win against
  a real foe; a cautious one a victory won shoulder to shoulder; a
  literal one only meaningful contact with the enemy. A hard defeat
  costs glory - unless he was outnumbered, which carries no shame -
  and out-bleeding the enemy 2-to-1 earns glory even when the field is
  left undecided.
  While he is aggrieved he attacks at +15% with no marshal of yours
  counted on the field beside him. Send him alone and he fights like
  a man with something to prove.

FREE ACTIONS: help, end turn, wait, retreat, economy

RETREAT RECOVERY (2-4 turns - command skill drives The Rally):
  After retreating, marshals are demoralized.
  BLOCKED: attack, fortify, drill, scout
  ALLOWED: move, recruit, defend, wait, change stance

═══════════════════════════════════════

response.message:
MUSTER — Ney (24,000; expect about 78,676 with the corps likely to arrive, up to 96,789 if all march) vs Mack (large force) at Swabia — the balance of force looks favorable.
  WILL JOIN — Davout: is willing to march if the roads allow — likely to make it in time (about 98%)
  WILL NOT — Soult: awaits explicit orders and will NOT march — order 'Soult, support Ney' and he will march
  WILL JOIN — Lannes: marches to the sound of the guns — the Roland of the Army — likely to make it in time (about 95%)
  WILL JOIN — Murat: will march to the sound of the guns — but he and Ney are at odds; expect about half his weight — unlikely to make it in time (about 18%); order 'Murat, support Ney' and it rises to about 100%
  WILL NOT — Bernadotte: hesitates — the I Corps weighs its own ambitions — a written order ('Bernadotte, support Ney') would likely bring him
  WILL JOIN — Napoleon: is willing to march if the roads allow — likely to make it in time (about 95%)
  The Emperor commands in person — every corps on this field fights +10% harder, if he marches.
  What Swabia can feed is not known — the province is unscouted.
  Every corps in the province shares the field — that is the design. Only a corps still adjacent can be held out: fortify him (1 AP) and he stands apart until you move him.
  (Standing orders decide who marches: 'Soult, support Ney' authorizes even a literal marshal to move to his guns.)


[Combat] Ney leads the charge! (Aggressive: +15% attack)

envoy_digest.headline: Hesse and Papal States write.
envoy_digest.deadline_note: Answer them here. Unanswered letters lapse when the turn ends, and a court left waiting will not raise the matter again for some seasons.

items.diplomat_line: Hesse, wishing to go unnoticed: "Hesse counts what a quarrel with France would cost and what an understanding would return, and finds his councillors of one mind. Sign the pact of non-aggression."

Cardinal Consalvi, serenely: "Rome measures powers in centuries and finds it profitable to be patient with all of them; an understanding with France costs the Church nothing that time will not repay. Open the borders."

response.message: Sire, I shall lay the offered terms for France vs Britain on our own table, court by court. We answer the dispatch from Britain with a counter draft, not silence.

per_court_acceptance.voice_line: Metternich regrets that Austria must remain… unconvinced — the terms weigh heavier than their defeat. He offers Vienna's compliments on Marshal Ney's laurels at Bohemia — compliments, he notes, are not a signature.

holdout_actions.label: Ease Austria
holdout_actions.description: Soften terms toward Austria to bring them to the table.

holdout_actions.label: Drop Austria
holdout_actions.description: Drop Austria from the settlement; they remain at war.

dial_actions.label: Press Austria
dial_actions.description: Press Austria harder — applies to this court only.

demand_suggestions.label: Take Carniola from Austria
demand_suggestions.reason_display: Carniola sits beside what we already hold; Austria would keep it only on paper.

demand_suggestions.label: Demand 300 gold from Austria
demand_suggestions.reason_display: Austria's treasury can bear 300 gold — priced to wound the purse, not the pride.

demand_suggestions.label: Demand 100 gold a turn from Austria for 3 turns
demand_suggestions.reason_display: A tribute of 100 gold a turn for 3 turns — collected quietly, resented slowly, and well within Austria's means.

demand_suggestions.label: Vassalize Austria
demand_suggestions.reason_display: At 24% of our strength, Austria is better acquired than argued with.

demand_suggestions.label: Subjugate Austria
demand_suggestions.reason_display: At 24% of our strength, Austria cannot decline a master; subjugation merely sets it down in ink.

demand_suggestions.label: Force Austria into alliance
demand_suggestions.reason_display: An alliance signed under necessity still signs, Sire — Austria's weight moves to our side of the ledger.

demand_suggestions.label: Offer 300 gold to Austria
demand_suggestions.reason_display: A sweetener of 300 gold — Austria's resolve has a price, and it is conveniently paid in coin rather than provinces.

demand_suggestions.label: Offer Bohemia to Austria
demand_suggestions.reason_display: Ceding Bohemia purchases Austria's signature; a province spent at the right table buys more than it earns.

demand_suggestions.label: Offer Austria 100 gold a turn for 3 turns
demand_suggestions.reason_display: A pension of 100 gold a turn for 3 turns — Austria's peace bought on installment, gentler on the treasury than the war.

deferred_marshal_petition.title: Marshal Davout seeks an audience
deferred_marshal_petition.body: Sire, Davout submitted a summary of his corps' service this season. It is accurate, and it is longer than it needed to be. The staff now speak of the quarrel openly — this is no longer a passing mood.
deferred_marshal_petition.speaker: Davout
deferred_marshal_petition.speaker_line: "My corps is in good order, Sire. It has been in good order for some time now."

options.label: Let it stand
options.detail: Free, and it fixes nothing. For 2 more turns he brings NONE of his 21,021 men to any battle Murat leads, and the quarrel may harden further.

options.label: Promise Glory
options.detail: His patience is bought — the grievance shortens by 2 turns, and for 6 turns the quarrel cannot harden further.

options.label: Rebuke
options.detail: Trust -5. The grievance shortens by 1 turn.

options.label: Give him a command
options.detail: Send him against ArchdukeCharles into Tyrol. A grievance ends on the field, not at the table — if he makes good on it, it ends for good. Giving the order may bring on a battle at once.

response.message:
MUSTER — Massena (31,689; expect about 39,714 with the corps likely to arrive) vs Archduke Charles (33,289 men) at Tyrol — the balance of force looks even.
  WILL NOT — Davout: is dug in and will not abandon his works
  WILL NOT — Soult: awaits explicit orders and will NOT march — order 'Soult, support Massena' and he will march
  WILL JOIN — Lannes: stands on the field and will fight beside him
  WILL NOT — Bernadotte: hesitates — the I Corps weighs its own ambitions — a written order ('Bernadotte, support Massena') would likely bring him
  Tyrol feeds 30,000 — the whole muster standing there would lose ~667 men a turn to short supply.
  Every corps in the province shares the field — that is the design. Only a corps still adjacent can be held out: fortify him (1 AP) and he stands apart until you move him.
  Lannes shares the field at Tyrol — his men will absorb part of any losses.


[Combat] Massena's DEFENSIVE stance hampers offensive operations (-10% attack)
[Combat] Massena leads the charge! (Aggressive: +15% attack)
[Shield] ArchdukeCharles's DEFENSIVE stance strengthens the line! (+15% defense)
[Shield] ArchdukeCharles's methodical defense is exemplary! (Cautious: +20% total)
[Terrain] ArchdukeCharles benefits from Mountains terrain (+25% defense)
[Combat] Adjacent allies bolster Massena's attack! (+4%)
Massena attacks with overwhelming force. ArchdukeCharles holds the line. Casualties: Massena's army 4,784, ArchdukeCharles 2,904. Both armies remain in the field.

[Vindication] Massena's concerns were justified. The defeat could have been avoided.
[Materiel] Guns, horses and stores lost with the fallen: France -239g, Austria -145g.

actions.message:
[Combat] Kutuzov's DEFENSIVE stance hampers offensive operations (-10% attack)
[Shield] Murat's combined arms coordination! (+5% defense)
Kutuzov engages in solid combat. Kutuzov gains the advantage over Murat. Casualties: Kutuzov 1,853, Murat's army 3,614. Both armies remain in the field. Kutuzov advances into Moravia. (904 lost to march)
[Materiel] Guns, horses and stores lost with the fallen: Russia -92g, France -180g.
Napoleon withdraws to Vienna after the battle.

diorama.observation: The Emperor watched this field. Reinforcements from Napoleon bolstered Murat's position — though Ney and Soult never arrived, Sire.
diorama.enemy_voice: Kutuzov: "The moment was measured twice before I struck."

reinforcement_messages: Bennigsen could not reach the battlefield in time.

actions.message:
[Shield] Bernadotte steps forward to cover Lannes's retreat! "Lannes is in no condition to fight - I'll handle this!"


[Combat] ArchdukeCharles's DEFENSIVE stance hampers offensive operations (-10% attack)
[Shield] Bernadotte stands firm against superior numbers! (Cautious: +10% outnumbered)
[Combat] Adjacent allies bolster ArchdukeCharles's attack! (+2%)
ArchdukeCharles launches a decisive assault. ArchdukeCharles gains the advantage over Bernadotte. Casualties: ArchdukeCharles 1,452, Bernadotte 3,282. Both armies remain in the field. ArchdukeCharles advances into Bohemia. (656 lost to march)
[Materiel] Guns, horses and stores lost with the fallen: Austria -72g, France -164g.

diorama.observation: Bernadotte stood alone, Sire. Ney and Soult never came.
diorama.enemy_voice: Archduke Charles: "Your marshals are bold. Boldness is not a plan."

response.message:
MUSTER — Soult (19,951; expect about 33,975 with the corps likely to arrive, up to 38,648 if all march) vs Kutuzov (29,243 men) at Moravia — the balance of force looks favorable.
  WILL JOIN — Ney: will march to the sound of the guns — but he and Soult are at odds; expect about half his weight — may make it in time (about 47%); order 'Ney, support Soult' and it rises to about 99%
  WILL JOIN — Murat: stands on the field and will fight beside him
  WILL JOIN — Napoleon: is willing to march if the roads allow — likely to make it in time (about 95%)
  The Emperor commands in person — every corps on this field fights +10% harder, if he marches.
  Moravia feeds 60,000 — the whole muster standing there would lose ~1,486 men a turn to short supply.
  Every corps in the province shares the field — that is the design. Only a corps still adjacent can be held out: fortify him (1 AP) and he stands apart until you move him.
  Murat shares the field at Moravia — his men will absorb part of any losses.


[Shield] Kutuzov's DEFENSIVE stance strengthens the line! (+15% defense)
[Shield] Kutuzov's methodical defense is exemplary! (Cautious: +20% total)
[Combat] Adjacent allies bolster Soult's attack! (+4%)
Soult's forces advance steadily. Brutal stalemate between Soult and Kutuzov. Heavy casualties on both sides: Soult's army 3,490, Kutuzov 3,684.
[Materiel] Guns, horses and stores lost with the fallen: France -174g, Russia -184g.
Ney withdraws to Hungary after the battle.
Napoleon withdraws to Vienna after the battle.

diorama.observation: The Emperor watched this field. Ney and Napoleon arrived in time to steady Soult's position. The field was held, nothing further.
diorama.enemy_voice: Kutuzov: "Sit with me a while longer. Winter is walking this way."

battle_report.observation: Ney and Napoleon arrived in time to steady Soult's position. The field was held, nothing further.
battle_report.enemy_voice: Kutuzov: "Sit with me a while longer. Winter is walking this way."
battle_report.marshal_voice: Soult: "Both lines remain where they stood. Nothing further to report."

response.message:
MUSTER — Soult (27,690; expect about 52,026 with the corps likely to arrive, up to 55,565 if all march) vs Kutuzov (21,282 men) at Bohemia — the balance of force looks favorable.
  WILL NOT — Ney: is in no condition to fight
  WILL NOT — Lannes: is in no condition to fight
  WILL NOT — Murat: is in no condition to fight
  WILL NOT — Bernadotte: hesitates — the I Corps weighs its own ambitions — a written order ('Bernadotte, support Soult') would likely bring him
  WILL JOIN — Massena: will march to the sound of the guns — likely to make it in time (about 96%)
  WILL JOIN — Napoleon: is willing to march if the roads allow — likely to make it in time (about 95%)
  The Emperor commands in person — every corps on this field fights +10% harder, if he marches.
  Bohemia feeds 60,000 — the whole muster standing there would lose ~1,134 men a turn to short supply.
  Every corps in the province shares the field — that is the design. Only a corps still adjacent can be held out: fortify him (1 AP) and he stands apart until you move him.


[Shield] Kutuzov's DEFENSIVE stance strengthens the line! (+15% defense)
[Shield] Kutuzov's methodical defense is exemplary! (Cautious: +20% total) Outnumbered bonus: +10%
Soult attacks with overwhelming force. Brutal stalemate between Soult and Kutuzov. Heavy casualties on both sides: Soult's army 3,042, Kutuzov 4,291.
[Materiel] Guns, horses and stores lost with the fallen: France -152g, Russia -214g.
Massena withdraws to Tyrol after the battle.
Napoleon withdraws to Vienna after the battle.

options.label: Send as suggested
options.description: Send the proposal with my recommended terms.

terms.talleyrand_commentary: They desire territory we do not yet control. Conquer it first, Sire, and our bargaining position transforms.

options.label: Harsher terms
options.description: Demand more — risky given our weak position.

options.label: More generous
options.description: Sweeten the offer to improve chances of acceptance.

options.label: Adjust terms
options.description: Build the offer step by step.

options.label: Reconsider
options.description: Let me think about this.

proposal_terms.talleyrand_commentary: They desire territory we do not yet control. Conquer it first, Sire, and our bargaining position transforms.

commitment_conflicts.display: Russia sits outside your bloc. Peace normalizes relations with a nation resisting your European influence.

display_lines: A 5-turn ceasefire: fighting stops, and the battles fought so far are struck from the war score — if the war resumes, it resumes from nothing. The campaign ledger of provinces and dead still stands. No territory or gold changes hands at its end.
When it expires: peace if relations have healed to -60 or better — otherwise the war resumes.
Relations stand at -80 and will thaw to -65 by expiry — short of -60; the war resumes when the truce expires unless relations improve by other means, or a second truce follows.

diplomatic_dialogue.acceptance_warning: This estimate reflects current conditions, Sire. Much may change during my journey — a battle lost, a relation soured. I would counsel a wider margin if you wish certainty.

warnings.text: Russia's court sees the French-led alignment consolidating across Europe and will resist a cross-bloc agreement. Prussia is the decisive non-France slice of the bloc; letting the alliance lapse would ease Europe's pressure.

payload.command: Berthier, remind me what the Russians demanded at the table

response.message: Sire, I must confess myself quite bewildered by this inquiry—you speak of a table and Russian demands, yet my records contain no diplomatic mission, no proposal, nor any prior negotiation with Kutuzov or Bennigsen to which I might refer. Perhaps you wish me to undertake a diplomatic mission to Bennigsen at Hungary, or did you intend to ask about a specific proposal we should lay before the Russians? Might I respectfully suggest rephrasing your order as either "Berthier, conduct a diplomatic mission to Bennigsen in Hungary to ascertain Russian demands" or "Berthier, propose white peace with Kutuzov in Bohemia"?

deferred_marshal_petition.title: Marshal Bernadotte seeks an audience
deferred_marshal_petition.body: Sire, Bernadotte has expressed reservations about the recognition afforded to Ney. He requests that his contributions be... noted. The staff now speak of the quarrel openly — this is no longer a passing mood.

deferred_marshal_petition.speaker_line: "I do not complain, Sire. I observe that Ney's despatches are read first, and mine are read after."

options.label: Let it stand

options.label: Promise Glory

Sire — the state of Europe, plainly told.

  THE CONGRESS OF PARIS — 33 of 45 titled (1 held, unsettled: Vienna) · summon from the Cabinet (F1)

  Against Britain: the war turns against us (-9) — 0 battles across 12 turns.
    Britain's design: The Low Countries — They will not suffer France's bloc in Flanders.
    Their price: prepared to go as far as war — France stands in the way (weight 85).
  Armistice with Russia: 3 turns remain — the truce points toward peace.

  Third Coalition stands against us, led by Britain — its posture is DEFENSIVE. (Threat 97, Formed.)
  What stirred Europe this turn: Natural threat decay (-3); Scorned a peace overture (+2); Hegemony Passive (+1).

  Holland: loyalty 83, steady.
  Switzerland: loyalty 88, falling.
  KingdomOfItaly: loyalty 97, rising.

My counsel, Sire: the war with Britain turns against us and their court would name terms. Their court would haggle over a plain peace rather than refuse it. Ask while asking is still a choice, Sire — take the counsel below, or open the war banner and press Request Terms.

reinforcement_messages: Archduke Charles's forces arrived to reinforce Archduke John!
Massed effective strength: 9,371 (lead) + 13,719 committed (Archduke Charles) = 23,090.
His supporting ally lost 2,701 men.

actions.message:
ArchdukeCharles assaults the Franconia garrison! Garrison: 750 -> 375 (-375). ArchdukeCharles loses 252 troops. Garrison holds — 375 defenders remain.
[Materiel] Guns, horses and stores lost with the fallen: Austria -12g, Bavaria -18g.
Brunswick holds position at Berlin, awaiting further orders. (Current stance: defensive)
Deroy holds position at Munich, awaiting further orders. (Current stance: neutral)

fog_hidden_nations: Britain, Spain, the Ottoman Empire and 3 other courts stirred as well, but their formations remain beyond our sight.

situation.enemy_strength_note: (an estimate — 2 of 2 known corps read from stale reports; unscouted armies are not counted)

marshals.danger: Crowded — Vienna carries more corps than its roads can bear, five turns running.

marshals.name: Ney
marshals.danger: Morale failing (0) — the men waver. Two turns of drill would steady them (+10 morale; +15 with a training ground).

marshals.name: Murat
marshals.danger: Morale failing (0) — the men waver. Two turns of drill would steady them (+10 morale; +15 with a training ground).

turn_events.message: Construction complete: Supply Depot in Vienna!
Supply cost you 539 men, at Vienna.
Garrison at Vienna reinforced: 14,000 -> 16,000
Marshal Oudinot accepts his commission — he raises a corps of 5,000 at Paris.
Davout's resentment of Murat has cooled for now. What was settled between them at the staff table has not been.
Berthier reports that Soult appears envious of Ney's laurels — he has grown scrupulous to the point of reproach.

morning_dispatch.berthier_note: Soult nurses a grievance against Ney, Sire. The rivalry wants settling before it is tested.

congress_clock.line: THE CONGRESS OF PARIS — 33 of 45 titled (1 held, unsettled: Vienna) · summon from the Cabinet (F1)

war_objectives.text: War Purpose: Defense vs Britain — the homeland — 27 of 28 provinces held (ticking: +2, +1/turn)  |  Settlement: White Peace (-8)
War Purpose: Defense vs Russia — the homeland — 27 of 28 provinces held  |  Settlement: White Peace (+0)

diplomatic_events.text: Britain has offered terms to settle France vs Britain.
Talleyrand reports: 5 diplomatic points available (base 3, +1 skill, +1 authority).
Talleyrand's efforts in Russia continue. Relations now at -47.
Relations between Austria and France have collapsed: OPEN_BORDERS → PEACE.
Britain's gold reaches Russia — the subsidy stands at 200 this season.
Relations with Russia have improved significantly (+11 this turn).

deferred_marshal_petition.title: Marshal Soult seeks an audience
deferred_marshal_petition.body: Sire, Soult's dispatches have become unusually detailed — obsessively so. Staff report he feels his current assignment is... beneath his abilities.
deferred_marshal_petition.speaker: Soult
deferred_marshal_petition.speaker_line: "My orders have been carried out exactly, Sire. I note that Ney was given orders worth carrying out."

options.label: Let it stand
options.detail: Free, and it fixes nothing. For 2 more turns he brings NONE of his 22,880 men to any battle Ney leads, and the quarrel may harden further.

options.label: Reassign
options.detail: His patience is bought — the grievance shortens by 2 turns, and for 6 turns the quarrel cannot harden further.

options.label: Rebuke
options.detail: Trust -5. The grievance shortens by 1 turn. His patrols pause a turn in reluctant compliance.

options.label: Give him a command
options.detail: There is no enemy within his reach to send him against.
options.unavailable_reason: There is no enemy within his reach to send him against.

DRILL COMPLETE: Murat's training is finished! +20% attack bonus ready for next battle. The ranks steady with the work: morale +10 (now 10).
Garrison at Vienna reinforced: 18,000 -> 20,000
Soult's resentment of Ney has cooled with time.
Berthier reports that Soult resents Ney's laurels again, 2 turns after the last — he has thrown himself into his post with obsessive diligence.

headline.text: Sire — Britain and Spain have made peace without us.

morning_dispatch.berthier_note: A peace made without France sets a table we were not at, Sire. Note who gained.

congress_clock.line: THE CONGRESS OF PARIS — 33 of 45 titled (1 held, unsettled: Vienna) · summon from the Cabinet (F1)

war_objectives.text: War Purpose: Defense vs Britain — the homeland — 27 of 28 provinces held (ticking: +4, +1/turn)  |  Settlement: White Peace (-6)

diplomatic_events.text: An envoy from Britain has arrived with a proposal.
Talleyrand reports: 5 diplomatic points available (base 3, +1 skill, +1 authority).
Talleyrand's efforts in Russia continue. Relations now at -25.
An envoy from the Kingdom of Italy has arrived with a petition.
The coalition against France has dissolved — but Britain remains at war with us.
The armistice between France and Russia has concluded. Peace declared.
THE CONGRESS: Britain and Spain have made their peace without France. Both courts are spent; their side of the war ends while the greater war goes on.
THE CONTINENTAL SYSTEM loosens: 31% of the Continent's ports are closed to Britain.
The blockade of Spain is broken — her ports breathe, her crews may drill again.
Relations with Russia have improved significantly (+11 this turn).

deferred_marshal_petition.title: Marshal Soult seeks an audience
deferred_marshal_petition.body: Sire, Soult has filed his orders, his counter-orders and his objections in triplicate. The objections are new. The staff now speak of the quarrel openly — this is no longer a passing mood.
deferred_marshal_petition.speaker: Soult
deferred_marshal_petition.speaker_line: "I have made a full report of the patrols, Sire. There were eleven. There was nothing in any of them."

options.label: Let it stand
options.detail: Free, and it fixes nothing. For 2 more turns he brings NONE of his 22,520 men to any battle Ney leads, and the quarrel may harden further.

options.label: Reassign
options.detail: His patience is bought — the grievance shortens by 2 turns, and for 6 turns the quarrel cannot harden further.

options.label: Rebuke
options.detail: Trust -5. The grievance shortens by 1 turn. His patrols pause a turn in reluctant compliance.

options.label: Give him a command
options.detail: There is no enemy within his reach to send him against.
options.unavailable_reason: There is no enemy within his reach to send him against.

[Shield] Wellesley's DEFENSIVE stance strengthens the line! (+15% defense)
[Shield] Wellesley's methodical defense is exemplary! (Cautious: +20% total) Outnumbered bonus: +10%
[Fort] Wellesley's fortified position provides +8% defense!
[Combat] Oudinot's combined arms coordination! (+10% attack)

[Materiel] Guns, horses and stores lost with the fallen: France -31g, Britain -51g.

turn_events.message: Ney is now locked in intensive drill. Cannot receive orders until training completes.
Murat is now locked in intensive drill. Cannot receive orders until training completes.
Garrison at Vienna reinforced: 20,000 -> 22,000
Soult's resentment of Ney is set aside. He holds you to your word.
Berthier reports that Soult appears envious of Oudinot's laurels — he has thrown himself at his returns and his pickets like a man proving a point.
Berthier notes that Ney has grown restless — he has not seen laurels while Oudinot wins them. I recommend giving him meaningful orders soon.

headline.text: Sire — Austria and Bavaria have made peace without us.

morning_dispatch.berthier_note: A peace made without France sets a table we were not at, Sire. Note who gained.

congress_clock.line: THE CONGRESS OF PARIS — 33 of 45 titled (1 held, unsettled: Vienna) · summon from the Cabinet (F1)

war_objectives.text: War Purpose: Defense vs Britain — the homeland — 27 of 28 provinces held (ticking: +5, +1/turn)  |  Settlement: White Peace (-2)

diplomatic_events.text: Britain has offered terms to settle France vs Britain.
Talleyrand reports: 5 diplomatic points available (base 3, +1 skill, +1 authority).
Talleyrand's efforts in Russia continue. Relations now at -16.
Relations between Austria and Russia have collapsed: ALLIANCE → DEFENSIVE_ALLIANCE.
THE CONGRESS: Austria and Bavaria have made their peace without France. Both courts are spent; their side of the war ends while the greater war goes on.
The court of Sardinia eases over The House of Savoy Restored — an ultimatum is now the length of its tether.
The court of Sweden eases over Scourge of the Usurper — an ultimatum is now the length of its tether.
And 1 other court stirs at its own design.

deferred_marshal_petition.title: Marshal Soult seeks an audience
deferred_marshal_petition.body: Sire, Soult's dispatches have become unusually detailed — obsessively so. Staff report he feels his current assignment is... beneath his abilities.
deferred_marshal_petition.speaker: Soult
deferred_marshal_petition.speaker_line: "My orders have been carried out exactly, Sire. I note that Oudinot was given orders worth carrying out."

options.label: Let it stand
options.detail: Free, and it fixes nothing. For 2 more turns he brings about half the weight of his 22,520 men to any battle Oudinot leads, and the quarrel may harden further.

options.label: Reassign
options.detail: His patience is bought — the grievance shortens by 2 turns, and for 6 turns the quarrel cannot harden further.

options.label: Rebuke
options.detail: Trust -5. The grievance shortens by 1 turn. His patrols pause a turn in reluctant compliance.

options.label: Give him a command
options.detail: There is no enemy within his reach to send him against.
options.unavailable_reason: There is no enemy within his reach to send him against.

incoming_settlement_offer.talleyrand_text: Sire, Britain has dispatched a settlement of France vs Britain. No indemnity either way — the war simply stops, and nothing changes hands but the quiet. Mark this, Sire: Russia mediates, and an arbiter scorned remembers it.

options.label: Request Revision

options.label: Reject Offer
options.description: Decline the offer without further negotiation.

response.message:
MUSTER — Oudinot (4,541) vs Wellesley (2,999 men) at Provence — the balance of force looks favorable.
  WILL JOIN — Marmont: is willing to march if the roads allow
  Provence feeds 40,000 — the whole muster can stand there fed.
  Every corps in the province shares the field — that is the design. Only a corps still adjacent can be held out: fortify him (1 AP) and he stands apart until you move him.


Oudinot holds them at Provence while allies attack from Lyonnais! (+1 coordination)

[Combat] Oudinot leads the charge! (Aggressive: +15% attack)
[Shield] Wellesley's DEFENSIVE stance strengthens the line! (+15% defense)
[Shield] Wellesley's methodical defense is exemplary! (Cautious: +20% total) Outnumbered bonus: +10%
[Combat] Adjacent allies bolster Oudinot's attack! (+2%)
Oudinot launches a devastating assault! Oudinot gains the advantage over Wellesley. Casualties: Oudinot's army 420, Wellesley 1,007. Both armies remain in the field.
[Materiel] Guns, horses and stores lost with the fallen: France -21g, Britain -50g.
